races.name: Bettingsites.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: What A Tahoo
runners_data.note: In fine form (three wins from last six, including two at this trip on Good), jockey Warren Fentiman claims 3lb which matters at this level; a natural hold-up horse who will need to find a clear run from the rear but has the raw ability to finish strongly if the pace is genuine enough.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Trainer Gemma Tutty has gone 0 from 13 over the past 14 days and this 3yo has been finishing mid-to-rear in handicaps on Good; her true racing style is hold-up, and with the field stacked with closers she will struggle to get daylight, making her prospects in this shape very thin.

runners_data.name: Bust A Moon
runners_data.note: Showed a creditable third at Southwell on Standard (5f, her best recent effort) but the 26-day absence and a pattern of double-figure finishes on this track temper enthusiasm; naturally a hold-up horse, she will be at the back of a crowded rear group and needs a faster pace than Startling is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: Poetic Jack
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran with solid placed form but has been finishing 6th-8th consistently in recent starts, and with headgear (p) having failed to spark a revival, there is little to suggest a breakthrough here; a confirmed hold-up type who will sit last or near-last, needing a strong pace he is unlikely to receive today.

runners_data.name: Mimime
runners_data.note: The 17-day turnaround is manageable and Luke Morris is a positive booking, but a sequence of 7th-10th finishes on both Good and Standard suggests limited headroom from OR 45 even in this company; wearing a hood, she is naturally a hold-up horse racing in a group of closers where clear runs will be at a premium.

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: The one genuine front-runner in the field and the key tactical factor in this race; consistent placed form (five times second in last five starts, one win on Standard) shows it performs best when able to control tempo, and Jason Hart's handling will be crucial in judging how much to conserve — the lone-leader role suits it perfectly even if the STYLE_FIT tag notes it ideally prefers a companion to race against.

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's runner arrives on the back of a 0 from 20 trainer run-rate over 14 days, but the horse itself has 1W2P from six Southwell starts (5f, Good/Standard) and James Sullivan knows the track; a hold-up horse by style who, given the quality of its course form relative to rivals, is the most likely of the closers to secure a handy position and mount a realistic late challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Startling is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will stride into an uncontested position from the outset on this flat Southwell 5f, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop at Standard pace. The remainder of the field — Gwen Tennyson, Bust A Moon, Poetic Jack, Mimime, Invincible Crown and What A Tahoo — are all natural hold-up or rear-of-field types, meaning the pack will bunch behind Startling with little pressure applied early. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, so Invincible Crown (strong recent course form and the highest ability marker among the closers) and What A Tahoo (in-form, proven on similar going) are the most likely to secure a prominent pitch just off the leader, while the true backmarkers — Bust A Moon, Poetic Jack and Mimime — will be shuffled further back than ideal. This race shape heavily favours a front-runner who can dictate and conserve energy, or a horse smart enough to sit second and sprint from close range; deep closers face a significant disadvantage with a single, slow-burning pace-setter unlikely to set up a strong enough gallop to be overhauled late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Startling Leads And Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Startling dictates a measured, uncontested gallop and the backmarkers fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Startling, with no pace rival to force an honest clip, sets its own rhythm and reaches the rising ground into the finish with reserves intact; its consistent placed form (five seconds from last five runs, one win on similar going) makes it ideally suited to this lone-leader shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Startling's pace proves too conservative and a sustained late surge from the hold-up pack catches it in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: What A Tahoo and Invincible Crown, both with winning form at this course and distance on Standard, possess the strongest finishing profiles and would benefit most if the race is run at a genuinely slow tempo that compresses the field; however, the redistributed hold-up types who must race out of role make a wholesale late surge less likely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse breaks sharply and secures a tracking position just behind Startling, effectively racing as a de facto second-speed horse.
scenarios.body: Invincible Crown has the course-and-distance record (1W2P from 6 runs at this track) and the weight to sit close, making it the best-placed to ambush Startling if it can find an early pitch; What A Tahoo's recent winning run at this trip on Standard also places it in the picture if it travels prominently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Fails To Fire
scenarios.trigger: If a messy break or blanket slow pace leaves the whole field flat and performance levels below par across the board.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types racing out of role and bunched in unfamiliar positions, interference or traffic problems could suppress the result and produce a below-form winner; Startling or Invincible Crown, as the two horses with the most tactical flexibility, still represent the likeliest beneficiaries of a muddled outcome.

watchPoints.text: Startling's early sectionals are the race — if Jason Hart allows the tempo to drop too low, the massed hold-up pack behind has enough numbers to overwhelm it in the final furlong regardless of its lead.

Invincible Crown's draw and break are worth tracking at the start; if James Sullivan can slot it directly into second place tracking Startling, it becomes a major danger rather than a standard late-closer given its superior Southwell record.

With five genuine hold-up horses in a field of seven all seeking the same late ground, traffic congestion in the straight is a real risk — watch for What A Tahoo and Bust A Moon in particular being baulked or switched wide in the final two furlongs.

Trainer Gemma Tutty's poor 14-day strike rate (0/13) is worth noting for Gwen Tennyson, as the horse has shown no winning form on any going and faces a race shape that does nothing to help a true rear-of-field type whose redistribution to midfield is cosmetic rather than real.

races.name: Bettingsites.co.uk Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Blue Moon Diamond
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and completely unknown in terms of running style — trainer Joey Ramsden sends this horse 0/3 in the recent 14-day window, no public form to assess, making its pace role entirely speculative and its chance hard to frame with any confidence.

runners_data.name: Miss Veronika
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's four-year-old holds one piece of similar-going form at Southwell (finished fourth) but her hold-up style is a structural mismatch for an uncontested 5f where the pace is unlikely to collapse; only 14 days since last run is fine but her profile is fundamentally at odds with this race shape.

runners_data.name: Atomik
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, though the map places it in midfield because the rear is already congested; in practice, its only start (seventh over 6f on Standard) gives little encouragement, and racing in a position more forward than natural is unlikely to bring out the best in this horse.

runners_data.name: Black Orchid
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's three-year-old has been remarkably consistent with three consecutive second-place finishes at 6f, including one on Standard going, and Billy Loughnane's booking is positive; unknown running style (U) but the placed record suggests a horse that travels prominently, and if it slots in behind Elyam it is the most likely beneficiary should the leader tire.

runners_data.name: Gris De Chine
runners_data.note: Zoe Hawkins's three-year-old has decent course experience with three runs on Standard going and finished third over this 5f trip before; Callum Hutchinson takes over in the saddle, and while form reads as mid-division finishes, the experience at this venue is a genuine asset in an open novice field.

runners_data.name: Beautiful Rumour
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a serious concern in a 5f race where there is no room to recover ground — and the nine-of-nine debut on Standard going at 6f provides no encouragement; Scott Dixon sends this runner into a race shape that is unlikely to suit a hold-up type that also shows a tendency to weaken late.

runners_data.name: Elyam
runners_data.note: Jason Hart's four-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner, the key figure in the pace map, but returns after a 740-day absence which introduces a significant fitness unknown; the tactical advantage of leading unchallenged over 5f on Fibresand is substantial, but whether this horse is race-ready after such a long layoff is the central question of the race.

races.paceDynamic: Elyam is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with 740 days off the track, will likely be allowed to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop over this standard-going Fibresand 5f at Southwell. With no genuine challenger for the lead, Elyam shapes to control tempo from the gates, setting an honest but manageable pace that is unlikely to stretch the field into a true test of stamina. The hold-up brigade — Miss Veronika, Beautiful Rumour, and Atomik — will be chasing from well off the pace, and on a flat 5f track where momentum is hard to build quickly, late closers face a significant ask against a well-positioned leader. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace, able to slot in behind Elyam and pounce without needing to make up significant ground; pure hold-up types are at a structural disadvantage. The field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate naturally — Atomik is redistributed to midfield on the map, but its true preference is for a closer's role; Elyam and Black Orchid are the horses most likely to naturally secure forward positions from the draw.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Elyam Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Elyam bowls clear from the gates and is allowed to dictate a fair but uncontested gallop, the race is run entirely to his strengths.
scenarios.body: Elyam sets the fractions unchallenged and, with 740 days off the track, the unknown fitness factor is offset by the massive tactical advantage of leading on a flat track; horses who race prominently can give chase but the deficit from hold-up positions is too great to bridge in 5f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Elyam's layoff tells in the closing stages and a prominent chaser overtakes in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Black Orchid has shown consistent placed form at this course and distance in similar going and, travelling just off the pace, is ideally positioned to exploit any fade from Elyam; Gris De Chine, with multiple runs at this track in standard going, can also land a blow from a handy berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and Elyam ties up, allowing a late finisher to close from deep.
scenarios.body: Miss Veronika or Beautiful Rumour would need the pace to completely collapse for their hold-up style to be rewarded over 5f on a flat track, which is structurally unlikely with only one front-runner setting a manageable tempo; even so, Miss Veronika's one piece of similar-going form gives her a marginal profile edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Elyam breaks poorly or checks early, scrambling the race order and producing a messy, contested sprint.
scenarios.body: Without a natural pace-setter to set structure, the race devolves into a scramble and any horse able to react quickly from a prominent position benefits; Blue Moon Diamond's unknown profile could be a factor as a lightly-raced unknown, while Black Orchid's consistent record suggests the temperament to handle disruption.

watchPoints.text: Elyam's fitness after 740 days off the track is the pivotal unknown — if he shows signs of tiring from 2f out, the entire race shape collapses and every projected outcome changes.

Black Orchid is sent off for a fourth consecutive race with a placed chance; if Billy Loughnane gets a clean break and slots directly behind Elyam, watch whether this horse can finally convert consistent placed form into a win.

Beautiful Rumour is flagged as a fader and is a hold-up type in a race with a single, manageable front-runner — monitor its market moves; if drifting, the "fades in finish" tag is being priced in by the market.

Atomik is not in its natural hold-up role and is effectively racing out of position in this shape — if Atomik appears to be forcing its way forward early, it could inject unexpected pace and briefly pressure Elyam before potentially tying up.

Trainer Joey Ramsden saddles two runners (Blue Moon Diamond and Atomik) with a recent 0/3 record in the 14-day window — watch for any stable information or significant market support for either runner given the low strike rate.

races.name: Bettingsites.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fiefdom
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Stuart Woods who steps up to 1m4f having shown ability over shorter on this Fibresand surface; sim-going record of 2/4 at Southwell is encouraging, and Luke Morris rides, but the 59-day absence and winless record at this trip are worth noting.

runners_data.name: Al Maslool
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained 3yo whose form reads well at 12f on Good ground, winning over that trip last time at Goodwood; Darragh Keenan takes the ride but this is a first venture onto AW and the surface switch from turf is an unknown that tempers confidence despite solid recent class.

runners_data.name: Mr Moonshine
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained 3yo who holds up naturally in the rear but is mapped to midfield here because the field's hold-up contingent is too large to all occupy that position — his sim-going record on comparable surfaces is just 1/9, which itself limits expectations regardless of where he ends up in running.

runners_data.name: Choir Boy
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain runner who wears a visor and has three Southwell runs on his card, giving genuine course familiarity; his true style is to settle and close, but with rivals occupying that ground, he may travel closer to the pace than ideal — the headgear change and fresh-ish preparation (17 days) are the positives to weigh.

runners_data.name: Grand Pier
runners_data.note: Won over 10f at Goodwood and filled the frame over the same trip at Kempton on soft, giving him both winning form and AW experience; Warren Greatrex is 3/9 in the last 14 days and amateur Harry Vigors (5lb claim) takes the ride, with only 7 days since his last run suggesting he returns in good order.

runners_data.name: Roker Roar
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's confirmed front-runner who has placed three times in his last five outings and carries the highest weight at 135lbs; his recent 3rd at Nottingham over 11f on Standard-equivalent ground is the most relevant piece of form, and Callum Hutchinson takes the ride with the key tactical advantage of uncontested lead.

runners_data.name: Much
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's tongue-tied 3yo with Billy Loughnane booked, whose best form includes a 2nd over 12f at Southwell — the most directly relevant piece of his record; he is a genuine hold-up type and will need the pace to be stronger than expected to close from the rear, making this race shape a tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Roker Roar is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a controlled, uncontested pace over this 1m4f Fibresand trip at Southwell, creating a genuine leader-dominant shape from the outset. Fiefdom and Grand Pier will seek to press or sit close to the pace from prominent positions, meaning the front of the race will be reasonably populated but not pressurised into a suicidal gallop. The hold-up contingent — Much, Al Maslool, Choir Boy, and Mr Moonshine — will be spread across mid-to-rear, though Choir Boy and Mr Moonshine are natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the field carries more deep closers than the rear can accommodate, and their ability to find their true position in running is not guaranteed. With one honest pace-setter dictating an even tempo and no genuine rival to force a breakneck gallop, this race shape heavily favours prominent-to-lead types who can travel comfortably in Roker Roar's wake and pick off the leader in the final two furlongs, rather than closers who need a strong pace to generate momentum from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Roker Roar Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Roker Roar is allowed to dictate a comfortable gallop and the prominent horses cannot close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Roker Roar sets an unchallenged lead at a controlled tempo, conserving enough energy to repel challengers in the Southwell straight, with Fiefdom and Grand Pier tracking but unable to quicken decisively past a horse with tactical reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Raider Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fiefdom or Grand Pier tracks the pace perfectly and produces a well-timed challenge to reel in Roker Roar inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: One of the prominent stalkers gets a golden tow into contention behind Roker Roar and finds the extra to collar the leader close home on the Fibresand surface; Grand Pier's recent course-adjacent form and return to a flatter track supports this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the leaders and a closer produces a sustained run from the rear of the field.
scenarios.body: Much or Al Maslool, both with staying profiles at 12f-plus, would be the primary beneficiaries if the fractions prove faster than expected and the front runners empty; however, the controlled nature of this pace makes a sustained late run from deep unlikely to be sufficient.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace crawls to such a degree that the race turns into a sprint from two furlongs out, negating running styles entirely.
scenarios.body: A muddling gallop collapses the field into a heap entering the straight, turning the finish into a short-distance dash where luck in running and raw sprint ability override stamina and positioning; hold-up horses redistributed to midfield are unlikely to benefit even in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Roker Roar — monitor whether Callum Hutchinson allows the horse to stride into a fully uncontested lead from the outset; if anything forces him into a faster early pace than intended, his stamina advantage weakens significantly in the closing stages.
Grand Pier — watch the market moves given Warren Greatrex's in-form stable (3/9 over 14 days) and the horse's recent win; if he is supported, he is the most likely to track Roker Roar and pounce.

Al Maslool — the surface switch from turf to Fibresand for this William Haggas 3yo is the single biggest unknown in the race; watch for any market signal that connections are confident about the AW, or for significant drifting that suggests concern.

Much and Mr Moonshine — both true hold-up horses in a race with a controlled front-runner; if the early sectionals on the Southwell straight are not genuinely testing, neither is likely to generate sufficient momentum from the rear to threaten the prominently-placed runners in the straight.

races.name: Bettingsites.co.uk Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Castlemont
runners_data.note: Won on debut at Goodwood over 10f in good ground, now steps up to 1m4f on Fibresand for Appleby/Loughnane; prominent style suits the predicted race shape perfectly, and the booking of Billy Loughnane is a strong yard signal for a single-run horse with a big reputation.

runners_data.name: Crystal Jet
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist with a win over 16f on Good ground and multiple placed efforts at staying trips; the switch to Fibresand is unproven but the distance suits and George Downing takes a decent ride if this shapes into the scenario that produces a late run.

runners_data.name: Lucy The Wire
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who sets the tactical agenda for the whole field; form figures of 4-2-2-1-8 include a Fibresand win over 10f at Standard, though the STYLE_FIT flag highlights she is stretching beyond her natural role here, and the trainer's 1/41 14-day strike rate is a caution.

runners_data.name: Arco Sancho
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed 3yo for Ivan Furtado with no public form on record and going marked as UNKNOWN — a total wildcard in an otherwise assessable field; Jason Hart's presence is interesting but the absence of any historical data makes this horse impossible to place with confidence on pace or ability grounds.

runners_data.name: Star of The Desert
runners_data.note: A natural front-end horse by inclination whose 0W2P record on Standard Fibresand is the relevant surface angle; pushed back to mapped midfield because Lucy The Wire and others fill the prominent slots ahead of her, meaning she may not get the forward position that suits her best, tempering her prospects in the most likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Walking On Stars
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 3yo carries a 6/17 14-day trainer strike rate that demands respect, and the horse's all-Fibresand form (2nd, 4th, 5th) over 7f-10f on Standard shows surface familiarity; a natural front-end type who will be competing for prominent ground rather than filling a midfield role comfortably, which is the honest caveat on her chances.

runners_data.name: Liam Mera Kai
runners_data.note: A 5yo with career form pointing firmly to soft/heavy ground conditions — every recent run has been on Soft or Heavy bar one — making this Standard Fibresand surface a significant query; the 107-day absence adds another uncertainty, though the step up in trip to 1m4f is something his 15f and 16f placed efforts suggest he can handle on a better surface.

runners_data.name: Maestro Del Mar
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from five Standard Fibresand runs including a 2nd over 12f and a 3rd over 14f at this course, which is genuinely the most relevant form in the race for surface and trip; a 7lb claimer in the saddle and a modest overall record outside his Fibresand niche limits confidence, but he is in the right environment to run his race.

races.paceDynamic: Lucy The Wire is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m4f Fibresand contest and should be allowed to dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Standard ground. Castlemont and Liam Mera Kai will press from prominent positions, but neither is a natural pace-setter willing to go toe-to-toe with Lucy The Wire for the lead. The field carries more prominent-minded horses than the race can accommodate — Walking On Stars and Star of The Desert are genuine front-end types by inclination but have been pushed back into mapped midfield positions because Lucy The Wire, Castlemont and Liam Mera Kai are all ahead of them in the queue for that ground; Star of The Desert and Walking On Stars are most likely to actually secure the prominent spots given their natural eagerness, though neither can displace the confirmed leader. A controlled, single-pace gallop at Standard Southwell over this trip is a shape that historically rewards horses who can travel prominently without over-racing and then sustain their effort through the final quarter-mile — hold-up horses relying on a late surge have less to aim at when the tempo is honest but unspectacular, making the race shape most favourable to prominent-to-midfield runners with strong staying profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lucy Dictates, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lucy The Wire is allowed an uncontested lead and the pace stays controlled through the first mile.
scenarios.body: Lucy The Wire sets a sustainable gallop that strings the field out without burning them off, bringing prominent trackers into contention turning for home; horses with proven stamina at this trip who have been travelling just behind the pace inherit the advantage in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent War Quickens Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Star of The Desert or Walking On Stars refuse to settle and press Lucy The Wire, lifting the early fractions.
scenarios.body: A faster early pace stretches the field sooner and tests the stamina of every horse chasing; hold-up horses Crystal Jet and Maestro Del Mar, who would otherwise lack a target, get a stronger gallop to close into in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses significantly in the final quarter-mile, creating a truly strong late run opportunity.
scenarios.body: Crystal Jet, the most natural hold-up type in the field with multiple wins over middle-distances, would be best placed to reel in a tiring leader; Maestro Del Mar's Fibresand form (placed in two of five Standard runs) gives him a surface angle if he gets the right late-race conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Arco Sancho, an unknown quantity with no public form, proves significantly ahead of assessments and leads the market astray.
scenarios.body: The complete absence of public form history for Arco Sancho is the key variable — a Charlie Appleby-style debutant with a big reputation could dominate but for Ivan Furtado it represents a significant unknown; a field of moderate novices at Standard Southwell means even a moderately well-handicapped newcomer could exploit an unsettled pace map.

watchPoints.text: Lucy The Wire's ability to control the gallop unchallenged will determine the entire race shape — watch whether Star of The Desert or Walking On Stars go with her early, because if either does, the pace map shifts materially and hold-up horses Crystal Jet and Maestro Del Mar become live players.

Arco Sancho is a complete unknown quantity with no public form — watch the market moves and paddock behaviour closely, as any significant support for this Ivan Furtado runner would suggest private trial form that could reframe the race entirely.

Liam Mera Kai's entire career profile is built on Soft and Heavy ground, and every placed effort over staying trips has come in testing conditions — the Standard Fibresand surface here represents a significant step into the unknown and a big reversal of his usual form environment.

Walking On Stars and Star of The Desert should both be watched in the early stages to see whether they track up to Lucy The Wire or accept midfield positions — if both press for prominent ground, the front end becomes competitive and the scenario probabilities shift toward hold-up finishers.

Castlemont is a single-run Appleby debutant stepping from 10f at Goodwood to 1m4f on Fibresand — watch how he travels through the race, as his debut win gives little distance or surface evidence for this specific test.

races.name: Bettingsites.co.uk Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Luminare
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained 3yo with a solid prominent style and four placings from five similar-going starts (STA/GOO); 48-day absence is the main query but she handles this track and distance combination well, likely to feature prominently throughout.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Experienced 6yo hold-up filly whose recent form in similar company is modest (best efforts at GOO, struggles on STA — only 1W1P from 15 similar-going runs); tongue strap fitted, and she will need a stronger pace than Alterity is likely to set to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Enola Grey
runners_data.note: In excellent form on paper but her natural style is to race deeply held off a strong pace — the race shape here will not be what she wants, as an uncontested Alterity is unlikely to generate the tempo she needs; her STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 reflects the genuine positional mismatch, and her 0W record in 8 similar-going runs compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Great Mates
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides this consistent 4yo who won over this track and distance (1/8f/STA) and was placed again on her most recent Southwell visit; prominent racer with headgear (h) likely to land a forward pitch and is one of the chief dangers to Chantelle from that position.

runners_data.name: The Third Star
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up type for Owen Burrows, with two good seconds at Goodwood but limited Southwell profile; 56-day absence and the likely slow pace from an uncontested Alterity makes life difficult, though Callum Rodriguez is capable of innovative positioning.

runners_data.name: Chantelle
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 3yo has an excellent recent record — 2W3P from 5 similar-going starts — and runs in the headgear (p) that accompanied her wins; Luke Morris will look to track Alterity closely from a prominent pitch, and this controlled pace scenario is tailor-made for her style and form.

runners_data.name: Beauty By My Side
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up filly whose form figures on Fibresand are poor (average finishing position 9.4 from 5 STA runs); placed here on a claim, Mason Paetel (3) rides, but the redistribution means she races further forward than ideal and her raw form gives little cause for optimism regardless of position.

runners_data.name: Borjina
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 3yo is interesting — her sole Fibresand run produced a fourth (4/7f/STA) and she won on turf at 7f; Daniel Tudhope is a strong booking and if she gets a well-paced race she may be underrated, though her hold-up style in a potentially dawdling race is a concern.

runners_data.name: Alterity
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo front-runner won over this course and distance (1/8f/GOO) and arrives with no pace rivals to challenge her; Jason Hart can dictate every yard on Standard Fibresand and this uncontested scenario is the best-case outcome for a horse whose stamina for 1m has already been proven.

races.paceDynamic: Alterity is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jason Hart can dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop from the outset on the Fibresand oval at Southwell. At a mile on Standard going, this creates a sustainable rhythm rather than a gruelling test — the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the advantage for deep closers. Chantelle and Great Mates will press into prominent positions behind Alterity, while Luminare will also be forward, meaning the first three or four furlongs will be well-populated up front. This race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can track the controlled tempo and produce a finish, rather than hold-up types who need a strong pace to close into. The field contains more genuine hold-up horses (Enola Grey, Beauty By My Side) than the rear of the race can accommodate, and both are likely to find themselves shuffled further forward than ideal, but neither has the natural early pace to dominate — Alterity and Chantelle are most likely to own the first two slots heading into the back straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alterity Controls, Chasers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Alterity leads at a fair clip unchallenged and the race develops into a test of who tracks best.
scenarios.body: Alterity sets an honest but uncontested gallop and Chantelle, tracking sweetly from second or third, unleashes the superior finishing kick of a horse with a 2W3P record at this venue on similar going; Great Mates, also well-placed from a prominent pitch, is dangerous too given her Southwell form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Alterity Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Alterity is allowed to drift into a slow crawl up front and simply pings clear at the two-furlong pole before rivals realise.
scenarios.body: With no early pressure and Jason Hart able to dictate every yard, Alterity could produce a devastating front-running display at a distance she won over last time (1/8f/GOO), stealing a decisive lead before the chasers can respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Closer Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is genuinely slow, creating a sprint finish in which a hold-up runner makes unexpected ground from the back.
scenarios.body: The Third Star or Borjina, racing patiently from midfield, could find themselves with more to give in the final furlong if the pace implodes into a rough tactical crawl; Borjina's strong Southwell Fibresand record (1/7f/STA) makes her the more credible of the two.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Prominent Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Great Mates, Chantelle and Luminare all push hard for position and force a genuinely contested pace that burns out the front group.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early split would fatigue those stuck in a battle near the front and hand opportunity to any fresher leg tracking just off the pace; Alessia Fernanda, drawn back in the field, could sneak into frame if the front ranks tire dramatically.

watchPoints.text: Alterity (Jason Hart) has zero pace rivals — watch whether she is allowed to creep into a near-crawl through the first half, as a slow gallop followed by a sharp sprint-finish would suit her far more than the hold-up horses trying to close.

Chantelle is Sir Mark Prescott's bankers material — 20 days since last run, excellent STA record, prominent style suits the shape perfectly; any bigger-than-expected price would be notable given her profile matches this scenario almost exactly.

Great Mates (Billy Loughnane) has solid Southwell form including a course-and-distance win; watch the market — if she drifts significantly it may reflect concerns about the 44-day layoff, but her style and track record make her a genuine threat in the dominant scenario.

Borjina (Daniel Tudhope) is a horse to monitor if the pace quickens earlier than expected — her single Fibresand run left questions unanswered and Tudhope rarely wastes a journey to Southwell; any market move late should be noted.

Enola Grey and Beauty By My Side are both true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the pace map — neither will get the strong gallop they need, and both can be treated with reduced confidence regardless of their nominal odds.

races.name: Bettingsites.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hot And Cold
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with solid Standard-going course form (two wins at the trip on AW), ridden by Luke Morris for Sir Mark Prescott who operates at 6/17 over 14 days; uncontested lead is the expected scenario and at 41 days since last run the freshness angle suits a horse who has won fresh before.

runners_data.name: Franschhoek
runners_data.note: Won on Standard AW at this course and distance last time out, Billy Loughnane rides for in-form James Fanshawe (5/19 in 14 days), and only two runs in the book means market confidence will be the guide; the 1m trip on Fibresand appears well within range.

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: Veteran handicapper with headgear (p) and a big book of form, but recent outings on Good ground (including a 17th last time) are a concern; the move to Standard AW is a significant switch, though OR 74 gives weight-in-hand appeal if conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Hale End
runners_data.note: Prominent type running the same route as stablemate Roaring Ralph under Sean Kirrane, with Michael Dods sending out two runners (4/27 in 14 days) suggesting stable confidence is split; best effort at 8f on Good, 140lbs is the joint top weight, and Standard AW form is limited.

runners_data.name: Kalamunda
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with three AW wins at the trip and Standard-going form figures of 2 and 6 over this course and distance; 63 days off is the longest layoff in the field and Darragh Keenan rides for a trainer (Joseph Parr) at 1/5 in the past fortnight — quiet form signal.

runners_data.name: Kaleido
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-tie and has placed twice in recent outings on Good ground but all five recent runs came on Good — no Standard AW experience in the record; Daniel Tudhope is a high-class booking for David O'Meara (6/50 in 14 days), and a surface question hangs over this horse's chance.

runners_data.name: Savile Row
runners_data.note: Has course and distance form on Standard (3rd last time) which is a key positive; wears visor and tongue-tie, Harry Russell takes the ride for a trainer (Antony Brittain) with no wins in 14 days, but the proven Fibresand profile makes this a legitimate player from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: American State
runners_data.note: Ran 2nd at 10f on Standard AW recently so the surface holds no fears, but has been well beaten on his last three starts including a string of poor efforts at this course; Ivan Furtado's yard is winless in 14 days and the horse is mapped as a hold-up type who needs things to go right late.

runners_data.name: Double Eagle
runners_data.note: OR 63 is the lowest in the field and recent form shows a 9th at this course on Standard last time out; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, pushed into the midfield picture on the pace map because the rear is already crowded — racing away from his preferred position tempers expectations significantly.

races.paceDynamic: Hot And Cold is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to match them stride for stride from the gates, they should be permitted to control proceedings at a sustainable gallop on Standard Fibresand over this flat mile at Southwell. Franschhoek, Roaring Ralph, Hale End, and Savile Row all want prominent positions, creating a four-way congestion for the lead group that will generate significant traffic risk between the two- and three-furlong markers, even if the overall tempo remains measured. Kalamunda, Kaleido, and American State are the natural hold-up horses, but with Double Eagle also a genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield picture on the map, there is more pace and prominence in this field than the race shape can cleanly accommodate. The controlled, single-pacemaker tempo strongly favours resolute prominent racers who can tuck in behind Hot And Cold without being caught in the midfield scrimmage, with the cleaner air and early positioning of the lead group making front-runners and close-attending prominent types the best-placed stylistically.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot And Cold Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Hot And Cold bowls along unchallenged and the prominent group behind them gets tangled in traffic between the three and two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Hot And Cold sets a relaxed, controlled pace and finds enough in reserve to hold on as the prominent bunch wastes energy jostling for position; Franschhoek is best placed of those closest to benefit if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the tracking prominent horses — most likely Franschhoek or Roaring Ralph — travels smoothly just off the pace and produces a well-timed challenge inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The measured tempo allows a prominent tracker to conserve energy in the slipstream before sweeping past a tiring Hot And Cold; Franschhoek's strong Standard-going form and Billy Loughnane's positional intelligence make them the most dangerous vehicle for this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and the hold-up horses find an unobstructed late run down the Southwell straight.
scenarios.body: Kalamunda or Kaleido would need a messy, stop-start gallop to create the gap they require, but the controlled single-file pace makes a dramatic late swoop harder to engineer; American State's AW form offers some claims but the margin for error is slim.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Incident
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster causes a chain-reaction of interference two to three furlongs out, producing a chaotic finishing straight.
scenarios.body: A fractured race with horses checked or shuffled back would scramble the form lines and open the door for any horse who finds daylight regardless of style; the compressed, congested pace picture makes this non-trivial but it remains the least predictable and least likely clean outcome.

watchPoints.text: Hot And Cold — if they are allowed a completely uncontested lead at a crawl, the Prescott-Morris combination can steal this race and the hold-up horses will have nothing to close on.

Franschhoek, Roaring Ralph, Hale End, and Savile Row — four horses chasing two prominent positions creates a serious crowding risk at the two-to-three furlong mark; any checking or clipping of heels could end a runner's chance instantly.

Kaleido — Daniel Tudhope is an elite jockey booking but this horse has never run on Standard AW, and the surface unknown is a genuine concern that could explain a short market price or lengthen it considerably.

Kalamunda — the 63-day absence is the longest layoff in the field; watch the market closely, as a trainer who has had just one winner in 14 days and a quiet record suggests this runner may need the race to find peak fitness.

Double Eagle — mapped to midfield but a genuine hold-up type; if they drift back to their natural position from the gates, they will be last or near-last and require an exceptional closing run on a track where front-runners are favoured.

races.name: Bettingsites.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Ollie Pears with a solid record at 7f, recording three places from eleven similar-going starts; the 20-day freshener is fine but the prominent logjam means a clean passage from the off cannot be assumed.

runners_data.name: Tactical Blitz
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's runner carries a convincing Southwell win and two places on this surface — the match-winning form is clearly here — but an 83-day absence and a poor trainer 14-day strike rate of 0/8 means fitness is a genuine question heading into this.

runners_data.name: Exotic Baby
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has a solid 14-day window (3/23) and Faleh Bughanaim takes over, but Exotic Baby's hold-up style requires the pace to collapse rivals in front, and its recent form string shows little spark with a sequence of mid-pack finishes on this surface and trip.

runners_data.name: Chale Chalo
runners_data.note: Twice a winner and placer at 7f on Southwell Standard — the course-and-distance form is the strongest in the field — but back-to-back poor runs since returning from a break and a trainer 14-day blank of 0/7 caution against over-confidence on rebound.

runners_data.name: Piscean Star
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane, in good form, takes over for Ed Dunlop (3/19 in the 14-day window) on a horse that has already won and placed at 7f Standard; the 14-day turnaround looks sharp rather than concerning and a prominent style means it should be close enough to matter.

runners_data.name: Korbut
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 6/17 14-day strike rate underlines a yard in full flow, and Korbut's four consecutive placed efforts at 7f Standard confirm its aptitude for exactly this configuration; as the only confirmed front-runner it gets an uncontested lead, which is a substantial positional advantage.

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Kije
runners_data.note: Harry Vigors claims 5lb and brings a placed effort at 7f Standard into the race, but a natural hold-up style means a clean run through traffic is required; the 22-day gap is routine and the trainer (2/17 in 14 days) shows at least some form.

runners_data.name: Black Endeavour
runners_data.note: Mark Rimell's runner won at 6f on Good ground most recently and carries headgear for the first time on turf — the step up in trip and the absence of any placed form on Standard AW (0/13 similar going) are significant doubts, even with the form form uptick.

runners_data.name: Southern Warrior
runners_data.note: Olly Williams sends out a horse whose genuine running style is hold-up, though the congestion of closers in this field means it is unlikely to secure even that back-marker berth cleanly; a 0/1 trainer 14-day strike and the lowest OR in the field (61) combine to make this an each-way long shot at best.

races.paceDynamic: Korbut is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, Luke Morris can control tempo from the front at whatever pace suits Sir Mark Prescott's patient plotting — expect a sustainable, honest gallop rather than a scorching early fractions on Standard Southwell AW. Behind Korbut, Indefensible, Tactical Blitz, Piscean Star, and Black Endeavour all want prominent positions, creating real congestion in the first two furlongs and danger of scrimmaging between the 2f and 3f poles as those four jostle for the handful of seats just off the pace. Southern Warrior is a genuine hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the reality that the rear ground will be crowded with Chale Chalo, Exotic Baby, and Lieutenant Kije — Southern Warrior is unlikely to find its natural berth and its chance must be discounted accordingly. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner setting a controlled pace with prominent runners fighting for the chasing positions — strongly favours horses who can sit handy just behind Korbut in first or second position and quicken from a stalking role in the final two furlongs, rather than those who must come from the back through traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Korbut Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Korbut dictates a controlled solo lead and the prominent scrimmage settles behind him within the first furlong.
scenarios.body: Korbut rolls along uncontested and the race becomes a proper test of who can maintain proximity and produce a sustained run from 2f out; horses who travel smoothly just off the pace into the straight are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Heats Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the early positional battle between Indefensible, Tactical Blitz, Piscean Star, and Black Endeavour forces a faster early clip than Korbut intends.
scenarios.body: An elevated early pace compresses the field and stretches stamina reserves, meaning a horse with a touch more class or freshness who can switch off mid-race suddenly has an advantage as rivals tire in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to create a gap and a hold-up runner picks a clear passage between the 2f and 1f poles.
scenarios.body: Chale Chalo or Lieutenant Kije, sitting deeper, would benefit from rivals stopping in front of them if the early fractions were fast enough to drain the prominent types; this scenario requires both elevated pace and a clean run, neither of which is guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands Breakaway Prize
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes significant interference and a lightly-raced or well-handicapped runner slips the field unnoticed.
scenarios.body: Black Endeavour, stepping up sharply in form with a recent win to its name and headgear in place, could benefit from a muddled scenario if prominent rivals check each other; this remains a low-probability shape given the controlled pace most likely set by Korbut.

watchPoints.text: Indefensible, Tactical Blitz, Piscean Star, and Black Endeavour will all hunt the same prominent positions in the first two furlongs — watch for bumping and checking between the 1f and 2f markers that could unsettle multiple runners simultaneously.

Korbut's ability to dictate a genuinely comfortable tempo unchallenged is the fulcrum of this race — if any prominent runner pressures it early, the race shape changes materially and Korbut's long odds-on role as pace controller collapses.

Tactical Blitz returns from 83 days off for a handler showing 0/8 in the 14-day window — watch the paddock and early market move for any sign the yard is expecting a fitness run rather than peak performance.

Chale Chalo has the strongest course-and-distance profile in the field but has run poorly in its last two starts; a false start or sluggish break from its hold-up position could leave Jason Hart with too much ground to make up on a track where passing is difficult late.

Black Endeavour's headgear (hg:t) appears for the first time in this context — watch whether the application sharpens its early response from the gates, as it would need to be much more prominent than its AW form suggests to feature.

races.name: Bettingsites.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Papa Cocktail
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with solid placed form at 6f on Good and Fibresand; Jason Hart takes over and the course-distance profile is respectable, though sim-going figures show only one win in 15 comparable runs and he typically needs a genuine test to get involved late.

runners_data.name: Tyger Bay
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type who won on Fibresand at this trip and has placed multiple times; Seamus Cronin (5) is a useful booking and the short five-day turnaround is not unusual for this yard, though soft-ground form dominates his recent history.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer in excellent form having won last two starts including a 6f Fibresand victory; the visor goes on, Luke Morris is an astute pilot, and this is the horse best equipped to press Diligent Resdev and then out-quicken in the straight.

runners_data.name: Flowstate
runners_data.note: Prominent/prominent-pressure type with four wins from 15 Fibresand starts at 7f; the 181-day absence is the key concern but David O'Meara's yard has the firepower and Rawlinson knows the horse — very interesting if fit.

runners_data.name: Prince Of Pillo
runners_data.note: Fahey's six-year-old is a natural hold-up runner but the surplus of rear-track types means he will likely end up racing closer to the pace than he would prefer, compressing his margin for error; one win and three places from nine Fibresand runs hints at ability on the surface.

runners_data.name: Rock Opera
runners_data.note: Another Fahey hold-up type whose recent form shows back-to-back 0s; his last two Goodwood runs produced 11th and 13th, and he finds himself squeezed into a midfield map position he would not naturally occupy — the current form makes it hard to be bullish.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's five-year-old has won on Fibresand at this trip but recent Goodwood efforts were poor; the tongue-tie is applied and Tudhope is a top-class rider, yet being a natural hold-up horse shifted forward by the field's shape makes his task complicated.

runners_data.name: Beauzon
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with a strong Fibresand record overall but very poor recent form (three 11ths and a 6th); shunted into midfield by the redistribution and carrying 126lbs, he needs everything to go right to revive his chances.

runners_data.name: Moving Force
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR=82 with Billy Loughnane aboard, but only three placed runs from 11 similar-going efforts and none from the front; a 34-day break and hold-up style mean he relies on a true pace and clear passage.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who hasn't won recently and whose sim-going figures (3W6P from 15) suggest some ability on this surface; all five recent losses have come on Good or Soft ground so the switch back to Fibresand standard could help, but the form string 805660 is not compelling.

runners_data.name: Diligent Resdev
runners_data.note: The race's sole pace-setter and mapped as such, but a STYLE_FIT flag notes this is not its natural home; all five recent runs came over 7f-8f on Good ground and this step down to 6f Fibresand is a significant surface and trip change — Joanna Mason will try to exploit unchallenged lead but fitness and trip suitability are real questions.

runners_data.name: Kirkdale
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two recent Fibresand wins over this exact trip; Edward Bethell's four-year-old has strong course-and-distance form, the visor is fitted, and 145 days off is the main query — if fit, he is ideally drawn to slot in just behind the pace in the perfect tactical position.

races.paceDynamic: Diligent Resdev is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 6f Southwell handicap and should lead without serious pressure, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop that neither collapses into a crawl nor stretches the field. Modern Times, Flowstate, and Kirkdale are all genuine prominent types who will push forward early and should sit just off the leader's heels in a compact group, meaning the early sections will be organised rather than chaotic. The redistribution of Prince Of Pillo, Rock Opera, Dorney Lake, and Beauzon into midfield on the map reflects that the field holds more natural hold-up types than can realistically get their preferred position at the rear — in truth those four will be competing for space and may end up more prominent than ideal or shuffled wider. The pace shape — one leader, three legitimate prominent horses pressing from behind — creates a steady, honest gallop that will likely favour horses racing prominently with the ability to quicken in the straight; genuine closers will need to cover ground and should find the pace too controlled to generate a closing surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Diligent Resdev leads cleanly and Modern Times, Flowstate, and Kirkdale track efficiently in a compact group.
scenarios.body: The pace is honest but not brutal, with the prominent runners travelling through the race without burning petrol; when the sprint kicks in at the 2f pole, the horses who have been travelling smoothly just off the pace are ideally placed to assert.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Frontrunner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Diligent Resdev is allowed an uncontested lead and the pack fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Racing on Southwell's flat fibresand where solo leaders can set their own tempo, Diligent Resdev simply dictates from the front and the hold-up horses have too much ground to make up over only 6f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and the front group ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Although several runners have hold-up profiles, many are redistributed types who will not truly be tracking from the rear, limiting the pool of genuine closers; Tyger Bay and Papa Cocktail, if given a true test of stamina, are the most likely beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses clash for position early and inject an unsustainable pace that scrambles the field.
scenarios.body: A messy early battle between Modern Times, Flowstate, and Kirkdale could string out the field, advantaging a hold-up horse with a strong finish if the pace collapses; Moving Force and Dorney Lake are best-placed if carnage at the front creates a vacuum.

watchPoints.text: Diligent Resdev's solo lead will dictate the entire tempo — if Joanna Mason secures a stress-free first furlong, the whole field is chasing a horse who has set its own terms; watch how quickly or slowly the first 2f are run as this sets the race's final shape.

Kirkdale and Flowstate are both absent for over 100 days — if either blows up after a period off the track, the prominent group loses a key component and the race shape may fall apart in the final furlong rather than produce a clean finish.

Prince Of Pillo, Rock Opera, Dorney Lake, and Beauzon are all natural hold-up horses who cannot all park at the rear in a 12-runner race; watch for these four jostling wider in midfield, potentially costing ground and energy in the early stages.

Modern Times has won his last two including a Fibresand 6f success — if he travels smoothly just behind Diligent Resdev without expending energy getting position, he is the horse most likely to exploit the controlled pace.

Moving Force's top rating of OR=82 is notable but his sim-going figures (0 wins from 11 comparable surface runs) suggest he struggles to translate class to this surface — watch if Billy Loughnane tries an uncharacteristic positive ride to compensate.
